title: “Meet Me Halfway”: The Costs and Benefits of Bargaining
authors: Xu Zhang; Puneet Manchanda; Junhong Chu
eligible_reason: Structural model of buyer demand, bargaining initiation, bargaining success and seller pricing estimated by truncation ML, SMM and ML on transaction-level data from an online platform, followed by policy simulations (banning bargaining, ignoring loss-of-face cost). No binary staggered treatment and no DiD or event study.
design_notes: main.m loads transaction_sample.txt and survey_aggregate.txt (province-level bargaining intentions from a survey) and calls TRUNCATION.m, MSM_FBC.m, ML_BS.m and MSM_PURCHASE.m; SUPPLY.m runs the policy simulations via FOC_MC.m and PROB_PURCHASE.m. Regression inventory empty (MATLAB only).
data_files_note: The code reads transaction_sample.txt and survey_aggregate.txt, but neither file is in the archive (20 entries, ~36 KB, MATLAB code and an RTF README only).
data_provenance_note: Platform transaction data and survey aggregates not included.
screener_notes: No article text or PDF available locally (data/text/mksc and papers/mksc checked Nov 2); OpenAlex abstract read from data/frame/mksc.jsonl. Design read from the README and the main-results code; no package code was run.
